1  JUDGMENT

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.01.2024 at about 09.00am.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 27.01.2024 at about 09.00am the petitioner was going as a Pillion Rider in the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J-2830 along with his son on Belagur SH-152 Road, from his home/native towards Belagur for his personal work, when they reached near Hocihalli Gate, Kadur Taluk, all of a sudden the rider of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J-2830 rode the vehicle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, suddenly a street dog was came in front o the vehicle.
Hence the rider of the two wheeler applied break, as a result the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Kadur Govt.
Hospital wherein provided first aid then shifted to NH Sahyadri Narayana Hospital, Shimoga for better treatment, admitted as an inpatient, underwent surgery and discharged with advice for followup treatment.

So far he has spent Rs.6,00,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines,
attendant charges, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, he was not able to do his work and other work as before the accident.
He has sustained loss of happiness, physically and mentally, loss of amenities, loss of future prospects, decreasing in life span and also stained pain and agony.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy was doing Agriculture and Milk Vending work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and was contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motorcycle/Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J- 2830 and the Panchanahalli Police have registered a case against the rider of the Honda Activa in their Cr.No.9/2024 p/u/Secs.279, 337 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

5A. The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement by denying the entire petition averments and also denied the issuance of policy in favour of 1st respondent and in respect of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J-2830.
There is a non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.

Further stated that, as on the date of accident petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in the insured vehicle motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J-2830 and as per Sec.II of policy it is a libaility policy and the Vamadev vs Vinutha V V on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166949314/
2 petitioner was a pillion rider as per policy terms and conditions policy it will not be covered to the pillion rider as per policy Sec.II.

Further denied the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant.

Hence,
the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 27.01.2024 at 9:00am, on Belagur Road, SH-152, near Hochihalli Gate, Yagati Hobli, Kadur tq., due to negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J-2830 and in the said accident petitioner had sustained injuries?

Issue No.2: Whether the respondent No.2 proves that, the rider of offending vehicle was not holding effective and valid DL at the time of alleged accident?
Issue No.3:- Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If yes, what is the quantum of amount and who is liable to pay ?
Issue No.4:- What order or Award?

The Manager of the 2nd respondent has examined himself as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 and 2.
8.
The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by both sides counsel.

9. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Issue No.1 :In the affirmative, Issue No.2 :In the Negative, Issue No.3: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.4: As per final order, for the foregoing #REASONS#

He has duly cross examined by the counsel for respondent No.2 at length.
He has deposed that on 27.01.2024 he was proceeding in a motorcycle as a pillion rider and his son was riding the motorcycle.
At that time a dog came across their motorcycle, due to which accident occurred.
The owner of the motorcycle was his daughter.
There was 15 days delay in lodging the complaint.
He further denied other material suggestions of the counsel in the cross examination.

12. The PW.2 is Medical Record Staff at Sahyadri Narayana Multi Specialty Hospital, Shivamogga,

sentences.text: The official of 2nd respondent has reiterated the contents of the written statement in the chief examination.
He admitted that the policy was in force at the time of accident but it was a Two Wheeler Bundled Policy.
The liability of pillion rider is not covered, insured as taken third party liability, own damages, personal accident coverage.
Not covered pillion rider in Bundle Policy.
Further stated that, as per Ex.R.2 it is a package policy but, as on the date of accident, period of policy was a Bundled Policy.
He has denied other suggestions of the petitioner's counsel.
14. Before evaluating the evidence of the PW.1, for cost of repetition, it is necessary to reproduce the case of the petitioner.

On 27.01.2024 at about 09.00am the petitioner was going as a Pillion Rider in the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA- 66-J-2830 along with his son on Belagur SH-152 Road, from his home/native towards Belagur for his personal work, when they reached near Hocihalli Gate,
Kadur Taluk, all of a sudden the rider of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-66-J-2830 rode the vehicle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, suddenly a street dog was came in front o the vehicle.
Hence the rider of the two wheeler applied break, as a result the petitioner fell down and caused the accident.
15. The petitioner has totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle's rider.
It is no doubt the police have submitted the charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle after thorough investigation.

The spot mahazar appended to charge sheet indicates that the accident occurred on Kadur - Bangalore SH-152, at Hochihalli Gate, Yagati Hobli, Kadur Taluk, Chikkamagaluru, NH-48 Road,
the Dog came infront of the vehicle and petitioner applied sudden break and caused the accident.
It is undisputed fact that the petitioner has not produced the spot sketch prepared by the investigating officer while drawing mahazar.
But, only on this count, case of the petitioner can not be considered as suspected case.
16. It is the specific case of the insurer that the petitioner himself was ridden the bike and caused the accident.
It is undisputed fact that, the owner of the bike is none other than daughter of the petitioner and she is a police official.
Only on this count it is not safe to hold that the petitioners are created the documents by handing glow with the police.
17. It is further contention of the insurer that rider did not possess a valid driving license.
Further petitioner was not wearing Helmet as on the date of accident.

However, the material on record are Vamadev vs Vinutha V V on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166949314/
4 clearly depicts that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: So, it is indicates that the rider of the offending vehicle was in hurried manner and the Dog came infornt of the motorcycle, suddenly petitioner applied break and caused the accident.
Further, the respondents have not placed any iota evidence to substantiate the same.
And the police have not charge sheeted for the offense punishable under section 3 read with 181 of Motor Vehicle Act.
So, the arguments does not holds any kind of water.
The material on records are clearly indicates that the accident has occurred sole negligence on the offending vehicle's rider.
18. A perusal of the charge sheet, the police have submitted the charge sheet against the accused or rider of the offending bike.
The police have referred section 279, 337 of IPC against the accused.
The police documents are clearly discloses that the accident was occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is undisputed fact that there was delay in the lodging the complaint.
At this juncture, it is beneficial to refer the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of 1RAVI V/s. BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that "in accident cases, human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim cannot be dismissed merely on that ground although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases.
Delay in lodging the claim should not be treated as fatal 1 (2011) 4 SCC 693 for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof."
19. In the light of the Judgment referred to supra in RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The Contents of the complaint clearly depicts that the informant has failed to lodge the complaint immediately as she was busy in providing medical aid to injured.
So, the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.
20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in a decision 22018 (5) SCC 656 held "24.

It will be useful to advert to the dictum in N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd. v. M. Karumai Ammal [N.K.V. Bros. (P) Ltd. v. M.
Karumai Ammal, (1980) 3 SCC 457 : 1980 SCC (Cri) 774] , wherein it was contended by the vehicle owner that the criminal case in relation to the accident had ended in acquittal and for which reason the claim under the Motor Vehicles Act ought to be rejected.

sentences.text: The observation made in para 3 of the judgment would throw some light as to what should be the approach of the Tribunal in motor accident cases.

The same reads thus :
"3. Road accidents are one of the top killers in our country, specially when truck and bus drivers operate nocturnally.
This proverbial recklessness often persuades the courts, as has been observed by us earlier in other cases, to draw an initial presumption in several cases based on the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur.
Accidents Tribunals must take special care to see that innocent victims do not suffer and drivers and owners do not escape liability merely because of some doubt here or some obscurity there.
Save in plain cases, culpability must be inferred from the circumstances where it is fairly reasonable.

The court should not succumb to niceties,
technicalities and mystic maybes.

We are 2 Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd., emphasising this aspect because we are often distressed by transport operators getting away with it thanks to judicial laxity, despite the fact that they do not exercise sufficient disciplinary control over the drivers in the matter of careful driving.

entities.text:
Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The heavy economic impact of culpable driving of public transport must bring owner and driver to their responsibility to their neighbor.
Indeed, the State must seriously consider no-fault liability by legislation.
A second aspect which pains us is the inadequacy of the compensation or undue parsimony practiced by tribunals.
We must remember that judicial tribunals are State organs and Article 41 of the Constitution lays the jurisprudential foundation for State relief against accidental disablement of citizens.
There is no justification for niggardliness in compensation.
A third factor which is harrowing is the enormous delay in disposal of accident cases resulting in compensation, even if awarded, being postponed by several years.

The States must appoint sufficient number of tribunals and the High Courts should insist upon quick disposals so that the trauma and tragedy already sustained may not be magnified by the injustice of delayed justice.
Many States are unjustly indifferent in this regard."

25. In Dulcina Fernandes [Dulcina Fernandes v. Joaquim Xavier Cruz, (2013) 10 SCC 646 :
(2014) 1 SCC (Civ) 73 : (2014) 1 SCC (Cri) 13] , this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied"

sentences.text: The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of rider of the insured.
The materials on records are clearly indicates that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the respondent No.1.
So, I hold issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the negative.
22. Issue No.3: the claimant has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.10.

It shows that the claimant has sustained (i) A sutured CLW over th Left trontoparictal region,
(ii) Two abrasions on the left forehead, (iii) An abrasion below the left eye, (iv) An abrasion over the right side of cheek, (v) Tenderness, ROM, over the left shoulder and (vi) Multiple abrasions over the left knee.

So, I am of the opinion that though the claimant is able to prove that he has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident but he has failed to prove that he had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Considering the contents of wound certificate and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be presumed that claimant has taken treatment for above said injury and he got recovered.
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.13 for a sum of Rs.78,832/-.

Out of these bills,
Sl.Nos.6 to 11 for Rs.13,894/- paid by Arogya Bhagya Yojana.
So, these bills has to be deducted.

As such, the total amount of Rs. Rs.64,938/- will be considered as medical expenses and the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of Medical Expenses.
23.
The petitioner has not produced Discharge summary to show the duration of treatment.

Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by him and also amount spent towards treatment, I am of the firm opinion that awarding a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- as global compensation under only one conventional head meets the ends of justice.
24. The counsel for the insurer has vehemently argued that, the pillion rider has not covered under the bundled policy.

Before giving specific findings on this issues, it is necessary to elaborate the features of the bundled policy: "A bundled bike insurance policy combines both own damage (OD) and third-party (TP) coverage into a single plan, typically offering a one-year OD policy and a multi-year TP policy (e.g., 3 or 5 years) for new two-wheelers.
This means you pay for your own damage coverage annually, while the third-party coverage is secured for a longer duration.
This approach simplifies the insurance process for new bike owners, offering a convenient way to secure comprehensive coverage while managing costs.

25 . The insurance policy marked at Ex.R2 depicts that the owner of the bike has insured the vehicle for OD from 09.08.2019 to 08.08.2019 and CPA sum assured Rs.15,00,000/- from 09.08.2019 to 08.08.2020 and 09.09.2020 to 08.08.2021 only.

Vamadev vs Vinutha V V on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166949314/
7
The owner has paid an amount of Rs.657/- every year towards basic third party liablity, Rs.325/- towards Compulsory PA cover (Owner Driver).

As per the policy,
compulsory PA cover is covered only for two years viz.,. from 09.08.2019 to 08.08.2020 and 09.09.2020 to 08.08.2021
The accident was occurred on 27.01.2024.
It means fifth year of the policy.
The insurance policy itself clearly demonstrated that the third party liabilty for five years.
The injured is not rider of the bike.
The petitioner is pillion rider of the bike as per police documents.
The entire policy does not depicts that the policy would act as ACT POLICY for next three years.
But terms and conditions and nature of the policy has clearly depicts that, rider and pillion rider would cover for first and second year of policy only.
Hence, it is appears to Court that, pillion rider of the offending bike has not termed as third party in this policy.
Therefore, I declined to fasten the liability on insurance company.
So, I answered issue No.3 partly in affirmative.
26. Issue No.4:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimant is entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part against the respondent No.1.
Claim petition against the respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire amount with interest as awarded amount is meager one.
The office is directed to release the entire amount to petitioner or PW.1 with interest through e-payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/-
 fixed.
Draw the award accordingly.

Vamadev vs Vinutha V V on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166949314/
7
The accident was occurred on 27.01.2024.
It means fifth year of the policy.
The insurance policy itself clearly demonstrated that the third party liabilty for five years.
The injured is not rider of the bike.
The petitioner is pillion rider of the bike as per police documents.
The entire policy does not depicts that the policy would act as ACT POLICY for next three years.
